cards.headline: Crypto can pay you to hold.
cards.body: Some coins offer a yield for holding them a certain way. Done honestly it is real, but it is never free money. Every genuine yield is payment for a service you provide or a risk you agree to take on.

art.alt: Coins locked behind a small gate feed through a pipe into a modest sprouting plant bearing a few new coins — real yield earned by securing and waiting.

cards.headline: Staking is a job, not a gift.
cards.body: Many networks let holders lock coins to help run and secure the chain. In return the protocol pays them newly issued coins. That reward is a wage for real work — validating transactions — not interest conjured from nowhere.

cards.headline: Locked up, and at risk.
cards.body: Staking has real costs. Coins are often locked for a period, so you cannot sell during a crash. And 'slashing' can dock part of your stake if the software you rely on misbehaves. The yield pays you for exactly these risks.

cards.prompt: A protocol pays 5% for staking. Where does that reward actually come from?

options.label: Newly issued coins for securing the chain
Free interest, like a savings account

cards.explanation: Staking rewards are new coins the network mints to pay validators for their work. It is a real, explainable source — which is exactly what separates it from a scam that cannot say where the yield comes from.

cards.headline: Ask where the money is made.
cards.body: A sustainable yield has a source you can point to: transaction fees, network issuance, lending interest. An unsustainable one is paid from new deposits and calls itself guaranteed. The test is simple — can anyone explain, precisely, who is paying you?

cards.title: What a real yield looks like
cards.caption: A believable 5% yield compounds steadily — real but modest. If a rate is many times this, treat the extra as a warning, not a bonus.

cards.headline: High yield is a question, not an answer.
cards.body: Rank yields by suspicion, not attraction. A few percent from staking a major network is plausible. A promise of double digits a month is a flare. The bigger the number, the harder its source should have to justify it.
A real staking reward is payment for helping [[1]] the network, which is why it comes with lock-ups and slashing risk.
cards.explanation: Stakers lock coins to validate transactions and keep the chain honest. The reward is a wage for that work — and the lock-up and slashing are the strings attached to it.

cards.summary: Real crypto yield pays you for a service and a risk; yield with no explainable source is a warning.
bullets: Staking pays new coins for helping secure the chain.
Lock-ups and slashing are the real costs behind the yield.
The higher the promised yield, the harder the source must justify it.

art.alt: Coins locked behind a small gate feed through a pipe into a modest sprouting plant bearing a few new coins — real yield earned by securing and waiting.

cards.insight: Honest yield always has an address you can visit. When no one can tell you who is paying, assume it is the next person in line.
